title: Ethiopian Injera with Honey
community: All of Ethiopia — the sweetest injera preparation
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Injera with Honey — freshly cooked injera spread generously with raw Ethiopian mountain honey and a thin layer of kibbeh. The sweet injera preparation — eaten as a children's snack, a celebration morning treat, and one of Ethiopia's most beloved simple pleasures.
longDesc: Injera with honey is the Ethiopian equivalent of bread and butter with honey — the tangy injera and the sweet honey create a combination that works perfectly. The kibbeh (if used) adds richness. This is how Ethiopian children are first introduced to their country's greatest bread.
steps: While injera is still warm, spread honey generously across the spongy surface.
Add a thin spread of softened kibbeh if using.
chefTips: Warm injera absorbs honey beautifully — cold injera repels it.
Ethiopian mountain honey is the only honey that does justice to injera — its floral complexity pairs perfectly with teff's sour ferment.
cookingScience: The warm injera's sponge-like hole structure (produced by CO2 during fermentation and cooking) acts like a capillary network — the honey is drawn by capillary action into the holes, distributing throughout the injera rather than sitting on the surface.
sustainabilityTips: Two of Ethiopia's most ancient foods — teff and honey — in their simplest combination.
culturalNote: Injera with honey is Ethiopia's oldest sweet snack — before sugar was common, honey was the sweetener, and injera was the bread. This combination, unchanged for thousands of years, is still the first food that many Ethiopian children learn to eat independently.
